summary: The root فزز (fzz) primarily means to startle, to be startled, or to flee in alarm.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: فَزَّ, (A, O, K,) aor. فَزِزَ, inf. n. فَزٌّ, (TA,) He (a gazelle) was, or became, frightened, or afraid. (A, O, K.) فَزَّ قَلْبُهُ His heart heaved by reason of fear. (O.) فَزَّ عَنْهُ He (a man, O) turned away from him. (A, O, K.) And He separated himself from him, and became alone. (A, O, K.) فَزَّ, aor. فَزِزَ, inf. n. فَزَازَةٌ and فُزُوزَةٌ, He (a man, O) became excited with ardour, or eagerness. (O, K.) فَزَّ فُلَانًا عَنْ مَوْضِعِهِ, (A, O, * K,) inf. n.
فزّزهُ He (a man) rendered him powerful, or strong, and made him to overcome. (Ibn-'Abbád, O.)
افتزّ He (a man, O) overcame; (K;) or was, or became, powerful, or strong, and overcame: (O:) and ابتزّ and ابت ّ signify the same: so in the Nawádir. (O, TA.)

استفزّهُ It (fear, S, A, O) excited him to lightness and unsteadiness; unsettled him. (S, A, O, K.) وَٱسْتَفْزِزْ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَعتَ مِنْهُمْ بِصَوْتِكَ, in the Kur [xvii. 66], is expl. by Fr as meaning And excite thou to lightness and unsteadiness, or unsettle thou, when thou canst, with thy voice. (O, TA.) And in like manner, وَإِنْ كَادُوا لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ الأَرْضِ, in the same [xvii. 78], is expl.
فَزٌّ A light, or an active, man. (S, A, O, K.) And The offspring of the cow; (S;) [meaning,] of the wild cow: (O, K:) because of its restlessness: (TA:) pl. أَفْزَازٌ. (S, O, K.)
فَزَّةٌ A leap with disquietude [or fright ]. (TA.)

قَعَدَ مُسْتَفَزًّا [so in a copy of the S, but without the vowel-signs: in two other copies of the same, مُسْتَوْفِزًا, which belongs to art. وفز:] He sat in an uneasy posture. (S.) فَرَسٌ مُسْتَفِزٌّ لِلْوَثْبِ وَالعَدْوِ [so in two copies of the S, in art. طمر; in the O, in that art., مُسْتَفِزُّ الوَثْبِ وَالعَدْوِ; probably a mistake for مُسْتَفَزّ; app. meaning, A horse in a state of excitement to leap and run. ]

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
